title: Google Drive / File Sync
oneLine: Store immutable content blocks separately from mutable metadata, upload in resumable chunks, and synchronize devices from a durable change log with cursor-based delta sync.
opening: I would separate file content from file metadata. Clients upload fixed-size chunks directly to a block/object store using a resumable session and per-block hashes. Metadata tracks file identity, parent, owner, version, permissions, block manifest, and deletion state. A metadata transaction commits a new immutable version and appends a change event. Devices keep a sync cursor and request deltas after that cursor; a push channel only tells them that changes exist. Content-addressed blocks enable deduplication and avoid re-uploading unchanged chunks. Concurrent edits use optimistic version checks—merge when the file type supports it, otherwise create a conflict copy. Deletes are tombstones, old versions move to cold storage, and every client operation is idempotent.
ask: File storage, collaborative editing, or both?
Maximum file size and supported devices/offline mode?
Version history, deduplication, and conflict semantics?
scale: Large files require multipart upload; small-file metadata QPS may dominate content bandwidth.
Choose chunk size as a trade-off among dedupe granularity, manifest size, and request overhead—around a few MB is common.
A sync cursor/change log prevents full directory scans on every reconnect.

decisions.default: Immutable content-addressed blocks plus mutable/versioned metadata.
decisions.why: It supports dedupe, resumability, history, and safe concurrent publication.
decisions.switch: Whole-object storage is simpler when files are small and dedupe/delta upload is unnecessary.

decisions.default: Durable per-user/team change log with cursor; push is only a hint.
decisions.why: Push can be lost and devices may be offline for long periods.
decisions.switch: Periodic full reconciliation remains a safety net for cursor expiry or corruption.

decisions.default: Optimistic version precondition and conflict copy for opaque binaries.
decisions.why: Automatic merging arbitrary files can destroy user data.
decisions.switch: Use OT/CRDT/domain merge for collaborative structured documents.

decisions.default: Deduplicate within a tenant/security boundary using hashes.
decisions.why: Cross-tenant dedupe can leak whether another user owns a file and complicate encryption.
decisions.switch: Convergent encryption requires careful threat analysis and is often not worth the privacy risk.

deepDives.title: Atomic publication
points: Blocks may upload independently, but a metadata transaction makes a complete version visible.
Unreferenced blocks are garbage-collected after a grace period.
Manifest and content hashes protect integrity.

deepDives.title: Permissions
points: Authorize every metadata/content reference, not only folder listing.
Cache entitlements with version/invalidation and prevent stale sharing tokens.
Audit share, download, delete, and restore operations.

deepDives.title: Offline sync
points: Keep a local operation journal with idempotency IDs.
Replay against current version; resolve conflicts explicitly.
Use exponential backoff and bandwidth-aware chunk scheduling.

failures.risk: Client completes metadata before all blocks exist
failures.response: Server verifies referenced block hashes/ownership before atomic version commit.
Cursor-based pull is authoritative; reconnect and periodic checks fetch all missed deltas.
If-Match/version precondition, conflict copy or domain merge, and visible history.
Reference tracking, delayed mark-and-sweep garbage collection, and repair scans.

questions.q: Why is push not the sync source of truth?
questions.a: Devices disconnect and notifications can be dropped or duplicated. The durable ordered change log plus cursor is authoritative; push only reduces detection latency.

questions.q: How do you upload only changed parts?
questions.a: Chunk locally, hash each block, ask which hashes already exist, upload missing blocks, then commit a new manifest. Content-defined chunking improves dedupe when bytes shift but costs more CPU/complexity.

questions.q: How do you delete a shared file?
questions.a: Use metadata tombstones and clear ownership semantics. Deleting a folder entry may not delete content referenced elsewhere; garbage collection occurs only when no retained version references the blocks.

questions.q: How do you recover from a corrupt cursor?
questions.a: Expire cursors with a reset signal and run a bounded full metadata reconciliation or snapshot, then resume deltas from a new checkpoint.

mistakes: Treating WebSocket push as reliable synchronization
Overwriting on last writer without conflict handling
seniorSignal: Center the design on immutable versions, authoritative metadata transactions, cursor-based reconciliation, explicit conflict semantics, and safe garbage collection.
implementation: Presigned multipart upload to S3-compatible storage
PostgreSQL/Spanner-like metadata with version preconditions and change log
Kafka notification stream plus WebSocket/SSE hints
Local client journal and chunk hash cache
